vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: huo15-img-prompt
Version: 2.4.0

The Huo15 Image Prompt bundle is a comprehensive and legitimate toolset for AI image and video prompt engineering. It includes scripts for prompt enhancement (enhance_prompt.py), video motion planning (enhance_video.py), metadata extraction (reverse_prompt.py), and direct rendering via 10 different backends (render_prompt.py). While the scripts handle sensitive API keys (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) and perform network requests, they do so strictly to communicate with the specified service providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Replicate, Fal.ai, etc.) as required for their stated functionality. The code is transparent, well-documented, avoids dangerous execution functions like eval(), and even includes a safety filter (safety_lint.py) to prevent the generation of harmful content.

llm.summary: The skill's code and SKILL.md are coherent with a prompt-engineering / T2I-T2V toolkit, but the registry metadata omits many sensitive environment variables the scripts actually read and the package writes session files to the user's home — this mismatch and the wide range of network-capable backends deserves caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (prompt enhancement, reverse engineering, and direct rendering to image/video backends) matches the included scripts (enhance_prompt.py, enhance_video.py, reverse_prompt.py, render_prompt.py, claude_polish.py, safety_lint.py). Many env vars and HTTP calls in the code are consistent with supporting multiple backends (Claude/Anthropic, OpenAI DALL·E, Replicate, Fal.ai, vendor-specific keys and local ComfyUI/SD WebUI endpoints). However the registry lists no required environment variables despite the code clearly expecting several provider API keys and URL overrides — an incoherence worth flagging.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md describes CLI usage and an agent invocation pattern; it does not ask the agent to read arbitrary system files or secrets. The scripts do, however: they persist multi-turn sessions to ~/.huo15/sessions/, parse local image files/URLs (reverse_prompt), and will send prompts to external services when configured. The instruction surface is generally within the declared purpose, but it grants the skill discretion to call local servers (localhost ComfyUI/SD WebUI) or remote image APIs and to save session state — actions that change the runtime footprint and should be considered when granting access.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only installation), which is lower risk than arbitrary downloads. However the package includes multiple Python scripts (no external dependencies beyond stdlib by design) which will be executed by the agent. Because there's no automated install, the code will run from disk as-is; users should inspect the included files before running.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry declares no required environment variables, but the code references many sensitive variables (examples found in source: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY, REPLICATE_API_TOKEN, FAL_KEY, ARK_API_KEY, KLING_API_KEY, MINIMAX_API_KEY, COMFYUI_URL, SDWEBUI_URL, etc.). These are appropriate for the supported backends, but the omission in the metadata is a mismatch that could lead users to unknowingly expose secrets. The number and variety of credential names is high relative to a simple prompt helper; each grants the skill network access with the ability to consume API quota or exfiltrate data if misused.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (normal). The skill writes session files to ~/.huo15/sessions/ for multi-turn consistency and may cache usage metadata from API responses, which is reasonable for its multi-turn design. It does not request forced always-on presence or attempt to modify other skills. Users should be aware of the local session persistence and that any API keys provided are used by the scripts to make outbound network calls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This package appears to be a legitimate prompt-engineering toolkit that supports many image/video backends, local servers (ComfyUI/SD WebUI), and cloud providers (Anthropic/Claude, OpenAI DALL·E, Replicate, Fal.ai, vendor-specific endpoints). Key cautions before installing or enabling it:

- Metadata mismatch: the registry lists no required environment variables but the scripts expect many sensitive keys (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, REPLICATE_API_TOKEN, FAL_KEY, KLING_API_KEY, MINIMAX_API_KEY, ARK_API_KEY, etc.). Do not provide global or high-privilege API keys without understanding scope — prefer per-skill or limited-scope tokens.

- Network and cost: if you supply any provider API key, the skill will make network calls that may incur usage/cost. If you want to avoid network calls, use dry-run/backends like `--backend none` or avoid setting remote credentials.

- Local endpoints: by default it targets localhost ComfyUI/SD WebUI URLs; ensure those local services are intended to be called. Running the skill can send requests to http://127.0.0.1 if those services exist.

- Persistence: it creates ~/.huo15/sessions/*.json for multi-turn sessions. Review those files for sensitive content (prompts may contain PII) and clean them if needed.

- Audit the code: the code is readable and not obfuscated; nevertheless, inspect the included scripts (especially render_prompt.py and claude_polish.py) to confirm behavior and to see how they use any credentials you supply.

- Least privilege and isolation: run the skill in an isolated environment or sandbox if possible, and grant only the minimal API keys required for the backends you intend to use. Consider creating limited-scope API tokens, billing alerts, or read-only tokens where supported.

If the registry were updated to declare the environment variables it uses (and ideally to document which features require which keys), my confidence would increase. If you want, I can list all the exact environment variable names and file paths the code reads/writes so you can make a more informed decision.
